utterances.text: Why do we need his initially here?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please ask the interpreters to assist the Trial Chamber and the OTP, and translate the words from right to left, [B/C/S spoken]? Could we ask the interpreters to look at the image and interpret the terms for the benefit of the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters are interpreting only words that are spoken. This will be interpreted later on. So you would like to tender this document as evidence, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please, yes. Could the witness please date the document and initial it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We don't need his initialling. But who drew this picture, Mr. Karadzic? Your team?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: My team -- [Interpretation] My team, based on the documents provided by Mr. Suljevic's investigation team.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I said that I accept that it might be 50 metres, although this information is not contained in our report. This building is part of the television building which is connected with Studio C by a hallway or a causeway. That's where the bomb fell, and I believe that the passage is also connected to the buildings. As I said, I don't know and I can't claim that the trajectory of the projectile was, indeed, as it is represented here. The only thing that I can claim and that is true, in my view, is that on the flat roof of the passage, there was damage caused by the projectile, and this is this part here [indicates].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will be assisted in a second, and then I will ask to you use a pen in order to encircle all that. It will make it easier for everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Suljevic, you don't have to sign it. Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. First of all, for -- just so that it's clear from the record, this diagram relates to an incident which was in the indictment in this case as Incident 17 in Schedule G, and which has subsequently been dropped from the indictment. Now, if the accused is tendering this diagram in order to challenge the credibility of this witness, we suggest that the report produced in respect of this incident also be admitted so that if the Trial Chamber wishes to draw any conclusions it wishes as to the witness's credibility, it has the witness's report to inspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: A report on this incident was not admitted --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No, we've never tendered it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- pursuant to Rule 73(D) ruling?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's a fair comment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But we are aware that this is not in the indictment. However, the incident in the Safeta Hadzica Street cannot be understood without -- without this incident and its qualification Incident 13 on G list, which is part of the indictment, and now in the following presentation we will establish the link. What I'm saying is this: According to that report --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Karadzic, I understand your comment, but simply I think Mr. Gaynor's comment/response is fair enough. In order to admit this, for the proper assessment we need to admit the witness's original report in relation to this incident as well. Is that fair enough?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President, that was my point as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So can you give the 65 ter number? Do you have that for the report?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to receive another confirmation from you, once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, we'll admit this, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D527, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And then the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We'll provide the 65 ter number at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That will be given a P number, which is ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P1341.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I was just going to interject that it might be more appropriate to do this kind of thing on redirect examination in the future, but we don't have any objection to the admission of the exhibit. But sometimes if Dr. Karadzic can complete his entire cross-examination, it may be that some of these documents are offered by our side. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it's related to the admission of specific Defence exhibits, so I understand your point. Let's continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have we not admitted 09815 when we started dealing with all these documents? 65 ter 09851 [as interpreted], has this not been admitted already?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is Exhibit D526, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's one and the only report that Mr. Gaynor refers to. This has been admitted. Okay, let's leave that aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, do you agree that this is the position of the buildings, of the facilities?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is one whole, that all these buildings are interconnected, that there are passages connecting one to the other. I do not have a scheme -- the layout, but this is the TV building as a whole. So these are not three different buildings, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. But you will agree that the first impact was here and that the place of explosion was here, where it is marked?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that the impact is somewhere on the roof. I don't know whether it is more to the right of the roof passage or to the left. However, it was on the roof of the passage, because there was damage there. There was also an impact on the vertical wall of the building which was also part of the television building, and, finally, the final place of explosion is somewhere here by the wall of Studio C [indicates]. That's where the bomb finally exploded. However, here [indicates], the lower part where the projectile fell was lower than the entrance into the buildings. It was a somewhat lower part of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have problems probably because we speak the same language and because we are very fast. It hasn't been recorded that this incident, although it is not part of the indictment, is organically connected with number 13 on List G. Can this please be reflected in the transcript, Incident 13, List G. Scheduled Incident 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let's move on. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As long as it's clear that that's apparently a comment by the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the point of view of Defence, we have established a link, and we will demonstrate the link, and that's why we are starting with first things first. And the first thing is this incident. Can the Court please produce again number 09851, image number 3, I believe. Can the lower image be zoomed in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, do you have an explanation for this? The aerial bomb weighing around 300 kilograms, together with motors, at a velocity of between 540 to 720 kilometres, at a distance of not more than 30 metres, that it caused this kind of damage in this place at this kind of impact? Do you have an explanation?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, this was not an impact in the actual sense of the word. This is just a scratch, as it were. The projectile just scratched this surface. This is not an impact. This is just a scratch.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we return the sketch once again. I'm referring to the previous document, 1D2202, the one that we had previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, how do you explain that this air-bomb, which only grazed that roof and, therefore, maintained its velocity to a large extent, after only a very few metres it started descending, then it turned around 75 or 80 degrees, and then it ricochetted off the wall of the infirmary or this tall building? It ricochetted, as you had also put it in your report?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously, I'll be repeating myself, but I don't know. I'm not making any assertions. I did not say that the projectile had this kind of a trajectory after touching the roof of the passage. I said that I accepted that it was 50 metres, but I did not measure it, so I don't know. I also don't know what the velocity was. Obviously, that was the range of the projectile somewhere around there. It had to fall there, because it had already reached the surface as soon as it touched the passage. So with that altitude, that was its ultimate range. So I'm not confirming that the projectile had this trajectory. Perhaps this can be an approximation of sorts. I said that I am just confirming these three points that were identified in the report and that are from the projectile when impacting the vertical wall and when falling on the surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you make a sketch or diagram?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did anybody else do that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. If there is a sketch, then it's got to be part of the file. As I said, I did not take part in the photo documentation that was compiled, and we see that it does exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In order to assist all the participants in these proceedings, do you believe that it should be explained how this projectile, as it made initial contact with the passage, ended up on the other side of the wall of Studio C, and this imagined trajectory or assumed trajectory has to be visualised taking into account the angle, the mass, inertia, all of that put together? Do you think that all of that was not necessary? How can we explain that the bomb from here ended up on this wall of Studio C?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that we did not do that. Again, that was not our task. I am not confirming this trajectory. There is a high degree of probability, but now we are discussing probability, that this projectile did not fly through the air from that wall, or, rather, to the wall of Studio C. Possibly, it fell somewhere around the middle, and perhaps it rolled on the ground. But all of this is purely theoretical, and I don't want to engage in that kind of theoretical guess-work. However, I cannot confirm that this is the trajectory of the projectile in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you confirm the mutual relationship between these buildings?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the positions of parts of these buildings, yes, but all of these are actually parts of one and the same building that are interconnected. As we've already said, it is not several buildings that are involved here. The RTV building is a very characteristic one. It has several different entities that are all interconnected.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: However, obviously, Studio C and the multi-storey building are not connected here, but somewhere else. There is a distance between them here, and the bomb moved from the multi-storey building to Studio C; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Also, in this part between Studio C and the passageway, there is some kind of a passageway?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I now ask you to take a blue marker and to draw your findings on this image, how the bomb got to this opposite wall of Studio C?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm going to repeat that I can just confirm what is contained in the report; that is, the points of contact between the projectile and a particular surface. However, we did not establish the trajectory of the projectile, itself. So I can confirm --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There's been a great deal of discussion about this particular diagram. The witness has indicated what he can -- the information he can provide about the general nature of that diagram, and has misgivings about other aspects of that. I wonder if we're not risking embedding in the record a great deal of confusion and inaccuracy if we ask a witness to try to explain something on the basis of a diagram he neither created nor can confirm the accuracy of, beyond some very general matters, especially when the entirety of the report is coming into evidence or the actual report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we heard the evidence of the witness. I will leave it to the witness whether he can draw anything or not. If he cannot draw anything, he can say so. Mr. Suljevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this schematic or diagram, I can just roughly mark the points of contact of the projectile on the surface, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Excellent. That would be something as well. Could you mark, with a blue marker, 1, 2, and 3, and say what 1 is and what 2 is and what 3 is?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1 would be the initial contact between the projectile and the flat roof. I don't know the position on the flat roof, but, say it's somewhere around here [marks]. The surface where the initial contact was, somewhere around here [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly, Mr. Suljevic? Are you moving this point closer to the multi-storey building or do you agree that it's here, where it is marked on the sketch?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, we did not measure it, so I don't know if it's 50 metres or more or less. It's somewhere on the flat roof of the passageway. I don't know. I cannot remember now and I cannot say. Also, I cannot speak of the passageway, itself, because it's not a rectangle. It's a roof with -- well, a roof that has to do with what the entire building looks like. So it's somewhere around here [marks], or left or right. I don't know whether it's to the left or right of this place that is marked as the point of ricochet. I don't know if I'm being clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Just tell me whether you measured it from the edge of the flat roof. Do you have these dimensions?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that this information is contained in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. So number 2, contact with the multi-storey building. Can you place number 2 there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere there [marks] on the vertical wall. On the photograph, that position can be seen the best, this second impact of the projectile with the vertical wall. Now I'm just going to mark the place where the explosion took place rather than where the projectile fell, because the projectile may have fallen somewhere between these two places. However, I think that this part of the passageway is at a lower level, and I think that the projectile fell here -- actually exploded, not fell. [Marks]. This is the point of explosion. This is the location where it exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can you give us the assumed point of fall where the projectile actually fell?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where it fell. It may have fallen and then rolled. I really cannot say. What I cannot claim with a high degree of probability, I would not like to mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put the date there now and your initials. And can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we just let it go, although this event is not listed in the schedule or it was redacted from the schedule of the indictment, because there's a point that it may go to the overall credibility of this witness's investigation. But delving in too much detail would be too much. It is also inconsistent with your allegation that -- in opposing the Prosecution adducing evidence as to the unscheduled events. So I'd like you to move on to the events covered by the indictment. Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. I was just going to note for the record, also, that this particular diagram, we don't have evidence as to who the author of it is, where or when it was created, or pursuant to which criteria it was created. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic confirmed that it was prepared by his team, the Defence, recently for the purpose of this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, by his team. But if it had been presented, for example, by the expert assisting him, perhaps he could -- this is the kind of evidence which could be brought in through his own witnesses. But while I'm on my feet, Mr. President: If Your Honours wish to know the 65 ter number of the report signed by Mr. Suljevic in respect of this incident, that number is 09868, should you wish to admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That was admitted as Exhibit P1341. We gave the number already.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, could you sign this document and today's date as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I mark something on this diagram? May I say that I don't know and that I do not claim that that is the trajectory, the red line, and also that I do not claim that this angle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we understand. Your evidence is in the transcript as well as in our memory, rest assured.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could this please be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The marked version will be admitted as Exhibit D528.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2201, 1D2201, could I have that, please. We would just like to establish these relations briefly, and then we are going to move on to the next incident, which is in the indictment and, in our view, is related to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You see this sketch, Mr. Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you know how high up this shell ricochetted on the multi-party -- multi-storey building as it was moving towards the Studio C?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you know about X? Do you know what X was; that is to say, the distance between the multi-storey building and Studio C?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that information either.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Was that spelled out precisely during the investigation?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said several times already, the part of the team that analysed the crater and collected evidence did not carry out measurements, so I do not have this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did anyone else do the measurements?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give an answer. I don't know the answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you know of any of these measurements? Do you know how far away the point of explosion is from the wall of this multi-storey building?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The center of explosion is right by the wall of Studio C; that is to say, it would be close to line X, the end of line X. Now, whether it's a metre or whatever from the wall, I don't know. I just know that on the wall of Studio C, there was this big hole in this wall made of reinforced concrete, and that is what I remember from the scene.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then there is no point in tendering this sketch, because the gentleman, the witness, does not know these measurements that are very important for us in order to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Move on to your next topic, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Can we have the previous document, 65 ter 09851, image number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D526.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Is this the place that we are talking about, the location of the explosion? This was taken from your findings, the passageway?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, and we can see in the background that there is this debris and the skeleton of a bus that used to be there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please have the next image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I told you to move on to the incident covered by the indictment. Unless you are going to show the relation between the TV building shelling and the number 13 incident, I would like you to --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so, Your Excellency, because our findings are quite different and they are very relevant to incident number 13; namely, to establish what exactly transpired here and how this relates one to the other. Could we have image 5, please, in e-court, photo 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your team established that the bomb exploded outside Studio C and that the blast opened the hole in the wall. Is that the hole that we see in this photo here depicted?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can see this dark blotch, and then we can see the reinforced wires of the reinforced concrete. The netting is broken, but it wasn't destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you please mark that, what you've just told us? Could you just mark it, and could you also show the direction from where the bomb came?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we see this, the reinforcement, the mesh, the metal mesh, and I will try to draw the lines to show where that mesh -- how it -- what it looks like. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you now please put your initials and the date?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Please tell us, because we -- before we tender this image: Would a bomb, which would roll to this spot, would it actually produce this kind of effect?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this is not just the impact -- the physical impact, the physical blow, but, rather, the effect of a detonation, an explosion of this bomb.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to tender this into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: There's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we are able to recognise those parts, I didn't see the point of asking the witness to mark it. But, in any event, we'll admit it. Let's move more efficiently, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D529.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, you are right, this is relevant. Could we now have image 6 or photo 6, please. Photo 6 from this same document. We've seen 4 and 5. These are 4 and 5, so I want the next photo, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that here we see shown the same spot, but the photo was taken from inside the building, and that we can also see this mesh, the armature of the reinforcement concrete?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Which way is the mesh bent? Or, rather, would you agree with me that there are two levels of armature here, because in a wall that is wide 40 centimetres, you would have to have a double mesh; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not a construction engineer, so I can't tell you, really, how many levels of armature they would have to have. But I do recall the width and the thickness of the armature, and it is bent towards the inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, but do we see it on this photo? Are they actually bent towards the interior or towards the exterior?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think this is towards the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, what about on the right-hand side, what we see there? Is that the -- does that show that that mesh is bent towards the interior?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can recall when I was there on site, it was actually bent going inwards. But on this photo, we cannot really judge that. On the left-hand side, perhaps, yes, but -- because we can see that towards the focus of the explosion, the crater, we can see that that is bent in the direction going inwards, and that's how they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could we now look at it again. Would you look at these -- the armature towards the right edge of the photo and at the bottom. Where we see this one piece of wire at the bottom, what do we see, this iron rod; which way is it bent?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that we can see, even in this photo, that they were bent inwards, and that's how it was on site when I visited the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: But, Mr. Suljevic, there are photographs, coloured photographs, which clearly show, and I think we can all see the armature on the right-hand side, that this one single wire at the bottom --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can see the picture, and then you can move on, Mr. Karadzic. I'm really doubting the relevance of this line of questioning. Move on to your point. Yes, if we zoom in on the picture, we can see what it is like. What is your next question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, just the general question. Do the bars -- or does the mesh always bend in the direction of the explosion or in the opposite direction? To be more precise, was it possible for this piece of mesh to actually bend in the opposite direction of the blast?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really wouldn't want to go into details and theoretical assumptions. But when there is an explosion, everything goes outwards from the focus of the explosion, and I can't see here any part of the mesh that is bent in the other direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please put your initials here and the date --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, no, all right, the whole document has already been admitted, so this is not necessary. Now I would like to move on to an incident related to what we've just seen here. That's the incident in Safet Hadzic Street that preceded this one by a month. I believe it was on the 24th of May. The 26th of May, I've just been told. And that is the Scheduled Incident 13 on List G of the indictment. Could you please pull up 65 ter 0614-9638. The document number, 65 ter, is 10273, 10273.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This has been admitted as Exhibit P456.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could we then have 1D2212. We can stay with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What do we see marked here? What buildings are these?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really tell, without being given some instructions, or landmarks, or some additional information. This is a part of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, am I correct in saying that this is part of the documentation relating to the incident in Safet Hadzic Street, number 2?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have the occasion to inspect the phone documents relating to this investigation at Safet Hadzic Street, nor was I on site.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Safet Hadzic Street, number 52.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I cannot find my bearings here, just based on the photos, what building exactly that would be.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we then have 1D2212. Could we just zoom out a bit, because the resolution is not very high here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, can you recognise what's in this photo? Do you know what part of town this is?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, instructed by or informed but what you've just said, that this is related to the Safet Hadzici incident, I know. But had I seen this photograph without any of that introduction, I would have no idea. But I assume that this is part of the Novi Grad municipality, the intersection there, the entryway to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can you see the TV building here in this photo?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In that case, if this is -- if these are the approaches from Stratinsela [phoen] and if this is the boulevard, the Mese Selimovica Boulevard, then that would be TV building. But we don't see the whole building, just one part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please now mark the television building using that pen?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is what I think it is, the Mese Selimovica Boulevard --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- this then here would be the television building, across the Mese Selimovica Boulevard. I think that is the building of the radio/television, because across from the television building there is a street leading from Svrakino Selo to Mese Selimovica Boulevard. I think that's what we see in this photo here. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please have 1D2175.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to keep this document he's marked?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, we could, but we'll probably want to go back to this document. But, yes, we could have it marked now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if this is Mese Selimovica Boulevard, if that's the street, then that is the television building, and that's what I would have -- that's all I'd have to say about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll admit this as Exhibit D530, and we'll have a break for half an hour. We will resume at five past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that Mr. Robinson has something to raise, or Mr. Karadzic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I wanted to explain to the Trial Chamber why I opted for the route that I did. The incident in Safeta Hadzica Street is represented in the indictment as an intentional shelling of a residential area by the VRS Army, and we saw and we hoped to be able to prove that what had happened during the previous incident that the OTP has excluded from my indictment means that it would be absolutely impossible for such a huge bomb -- for such a fast bomb to do pirouettes and to flutter, and that something different happened in Safeta Hadzica Street. The second thing that we are going to show, probably after the recess, is this: The zone where several incidents happened in Safeta Zajke Street, Majdanska Street, Safeta Hadzica Street, and Kalebidja [phoen], near the television, the one that we have just seen, this is a zone with several legitimate military targets; the arms factory, the wire factory, Energoinvest, Astra, the Geodesic Institute, the Municipal Assembly building. This is a densely populated area, but it is not a residential area. When the time comes, we are going to prove this. However, what we are trying to say here is that the way it has been represented, that the air-bomb ricochetted and exploded below Studio C, is absolutely not one and the same bomb. What happened in Safeta Hadzica, that's the bomb that had ricochetted from the passageway within the complex of the television building. So you can absolutely see, and we will prove it, that everything was done in a very amateurish way and that everything was misrepresented. And if we do not clarify all that, what remains is a question and a possibility that that shell had, indeed, been fired to target a residential area. However, Your Honours, when we shed more light on this zone, will you see that there are no residential buildings there, that all of those facilities are industrial facilities, most of which are legitimate military targets that were used for the production of military equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So to be clear, what you're saying now is what is ricochetted at the roof near Studio C landed at Safeta Hadzica Street; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. What ricochetted from the passage -- from the roof of the passage did not end up in the wall of Studio C, but, rather, in Safeta Hadzica Street. And that's the incident that we would like to explore within the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. That's your argument. Yes, let's bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. Suljevic. There was something we had to deal with in your absence. Mr. Karadzic, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the Court please produce 1D2175. 1D2175.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, could I please ask you to tell us whether you recognise this part of the city.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please recognise the television building, and can you mark it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are very good at it. Let's start it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The television building should be here [marks]. I don't know whether the facility comprises any other buildings. I believe it does. And this is the radio/television hall [marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can you please write that next to the drawing?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you please mark the building in Majdanska Street housing the transmission line -- rather, the transformer station.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what transformer station you have in mind. I don't where that is in Majdanska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you recognise Majdanska Street?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't say where Majdanska Street is. I don't know exactly which of the streets would be Majdanska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. I apologise to the interpreters. Could you please mark the building of the police station in Prvomajska Street? Currently, it is the Police Administration, Novi Grad, and the address is Prvomajska Street, number 21 or 22.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just can assume or -- it is probably somewhere around here. [Marks] I don't know whether it would be this particular building here or -- that's where the police station should have been or, rather, the Police Administration, Novi Grad. I don't know whether it's this building or next to it, but thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you please mark it with the letters "PS"?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that this "P" is on Majdanska Street, that this is actually Majdanska Street?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's Majdanska Street, then "P" is on it. I don't really know the names of all the streets. I know this is Mese Selimovica Boulevard, and where the police station is, that used to be Prvomajska Street. I don't know whether that's still the street's name. And if you're saying this is Majdanska, I'm not going to challenge that. But in that case, "P" would be on that street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you please mark the building of the Municipal Assembly of Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's across the road from the radio/television hall building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you mark that with the letters "SO"?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be somewhere around here, I suppose. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you please also mark the Geodesic Institute?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Geodesic Institute is adjacent to the Municipal Assembly building, and I suppose it should be somewhere around here. [Marks] First Municipal Assembly building and then towards the bridge is the Geodesic Institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Let's now use numbers. Could you please mark the radio/television building with the number 1?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, "1." [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Put number 2 next to the police station, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police station, number 2. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The Municipal Assembly building, Novi Grad, number 3.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The Geodesic Institute, number 4.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you please mark the Zica factory, the wire factory?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Zica factory is approximately across the road from the radio/television hall, but it is across the river as well. I don't know exactly, from this perspective, where it would be, but I believe that it should be somewhere around here, the facilities behind. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Put number 5 next to that.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you please mark Safeta Zajke Street for us?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember which street that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps it was Drinska at one point.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it was Drinska at one point, then it's above the railway line [marks]. Possibly that's the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you please put number 6 next to that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, number 6 marks Safeta Zajke Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And now on the opposite side, can you also mark Safeta Hadzica Street ?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is Safeta Hadzica Street. [Marks] I don't know how long it is. I really don't know how far it goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It goes in both directions, left and right.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't know how far. Yes, that's the direction of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you please put number 7 next to it? And, for the record, number 7 marks Safeta Hadzica Street.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And can I now ask you to mark the Energoinvest building?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which building do you have in mind, the transmission lines factory?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, between the police station and Zica.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I can pin-point the building. I can do it just roughly, because there is a testing ground for the testing of transmission lines somewhere around here [marks], and it's somewhere around here. I don't know which facility -- which building it is, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can you put a number 8 to denote the Energoinvest compound?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's somewhere around here. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can you please mark the Sik factory? As far as I can remember, it is a building adjacent to Zica, a building next to Zica.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, I believe that it is somewhere on this side -- on this side of the Zica factory. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Excellent, that's exactly how it was. Can you please put a number 9 next to the Sik factory, for the record?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you remember where Astra was? Astra was a very well-known building, was it not?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Astra was approximately across the road from Sik. I don't know how far from it it was or at what angle it was from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: But it was next to the Bulevar, was it not?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I think it was somewhere around here, possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you please put a number 10? It is probably a bit more closer to the Bulevar, but never mind. That's it. Number 10 is the Astra factory.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And could you now mark Uniklima and Igman at your furthest right side, if memory serves me well?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I am just marking locations, but I'm not sure where the facilities were. Uniklima was very close to Astra, as far as I can remember. I don't know if it was here, whether this would be -- no, this is something else. This is a city location. This is a public company, a public utility company, and Astra was perhaps to the right, and Uniklima perhaps would be -- [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. That's the complex. Can you put number 11 next to Uniklima, and Igman is below it, number 12?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What Igman do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The Igman factory in Kalica Street on the corner of Mese Selimovica and Alije Kucukalica boulevards.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not familiar with that, but I'm not contesting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Okay, let's forget number 12. Could you please initial the document, and before that could you please mark the building on Safeta Hadzica Street which was hit?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't, because I was not at the incident site in Hadzica Street, so I don't know which building had been hit. I do not want to speculate which one of the buildings was hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And can you identify the Safeta Zajke Street building that was hit?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in Safeta Zajke Street at the place of the incident, so I can't identify that building, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And can I ask you to look at the localities that we have marked, and can you draw a circle to encircle all of them together?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you now put a date, and could you please initial the document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, let's describe the document. Mr. Suljevic, our witness, has encircled all the places marked with numbers from 11 [as interpreted] to 11, all of them around the radio/television buildings in the centre and all of the other facilities that we have mentioned. Thank you very much. Can the document please be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. I just want to do note for the record, Mr. President, that this appears to be a Google Maps representation of terrain from August 2009, and the witness has been asked to comment about locations in May and -- around May 1995. I simply want to note that for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D531, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Just for Mr. Gaynor's information, all of these buildings are old, and nothing has changed from that time. Can the Court please produce 65 ter 09809.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please refrain from making a speech. Your speech is of no point, unless you ask the question and you hear his evidence from him on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In that case, Mr. Suljevic, the situation as you see it in the photo, has it changed from 1995? In other words, did the same buildings exist then as they do now?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. There have possibly been some little changes. Some buildings may have been reconstructed, but I believe that the situation hasn't changed much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. The 11 that we have marked?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether Astra still has the same purpose, but, in any case, the buildings are still there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we have resolved this, Your Excellency. I think this is better now. Can we now see 65 ter 09809.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this appears to be a duplicate of 65 ter 16828, which has been admitted as Exhibit P1325.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, could you please describe this document for us? Since there is an interpretation, you can just give us a summary.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report on traces of an explosion caused by the fall of a projectile in Dositejeva Street on 16 June 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, we don't have the same document. This is 65 ter 09809. Is this possibly a 1D document? It is from the same batch, but it is the 65 ter document 09809. The numbers are different. The type of the documents may be the same, but the numbers differ. And the ERN page number ends in 256. 0037-5256 is the ERN page number. If it's not in e-court, could we please place this on the ELMO. Thank you. I believe that the OTP has the translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, could you present the document to us now?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report, an expert report, on the projectile traces that was referred to on the 26th of May, 1995, in a document of the Centre of Security Stations. The projectile hit the roof of a residential building in Safeta Hadzica, number 52, and that's where it exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that in the request dated the 26th of May, it is stated that around 11.30, from the west and south-west, a heavy projectile came; is that what is written here?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written, but that's the request. However, the request is actually dated the 30th of May, 1995. However, that is the data referred to in the request of the Centre of Security Stations that, while conducting our analysis, we simply copied out. This is the information that we had received.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. So why is it that they had asked for your findings when they had already determined the trajectory, that is to say, west/south-west, and how did they do that? How did they manage to do that? It's stated in the request, where the shell had come from?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the content of this document. I can't see what the request actually says, so I cannot answer before seeing that. After what I see written here, what was submitted and then further on as for the traces of the explosion, it is clearly stated what is sought through a particular request.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you please read the first sentence of the second paragraph?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The request states that: "On the 26th of May, 1995, around 11.30, a heavy projectile came from the direction of west/south-west.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you read the next sentence, too?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, we found an English translation of this document. We can put that on the ELMO, as you wish, whichever you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm wondering how can you put both documents on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We can provide it directly to Your Honours, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be most convenient.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellency, is that 02/4-233-442?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I do confirm that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So the request says that this projectile landed. How was it that they set this direction or trajectory? How did they manage to define it already in the request?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say how someone had determined a particular trajectory. It is true that it was defined in the request, because we did not write anything down just like that. But I don't know if they asked for our -- for us to confirm that. That is not what they asked for in the request. If we have the rest of this request, we can see what is actually stated in the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we scroll down a bit, then, so the witness can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So read what was found there.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that: "The following has been submitted for testing:" That is to say, collected on the spot and submitted. "Nine large metal particles," that are marked with a certain number, and: "Six smaller metal particles in a cardboard box without a lid." Those pieces were not marked. Further on, it says the request refers to a request to determine the type of projectile involved; that is to say, that they did not ask for the trajectory of the projectile to be determined.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: On the basis of testing the traces of the projectile, did you define the type of projectile that fell on this building?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I suggest that we have a look at the entire report? Things are the way they were stated in the report. I don't know what we wrote up finally. I cannot recall, after this many reports. I really was in no position to remember everything that was stated in each and every report. But I do stand by what the report says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we ask the OTP to let us have a look at this report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we have the exhibit number, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. I'm informed that it's part of P1325. It's on page 6 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we're going to have it in e-court; right? Could we please have the next page in Serbian to see what else had been requested. Then we want the next one, page 5, not page 2. Actually, can we have the same in English and in the original. It probably starts with the word "Findings."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can you tell us, briefly, what it was that you found here?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is page 2. A moment ago, we had page 1, where it was stated what had been requested, and that was the type of projectile involved. On the next page, we have the findings, where individual pieces that had been submitted for expertise had been dealt with. So in the first bullet point of the findings, you can see that what was submitted were the remains of a rocket motor, and it says what the length was. There's a general description of all these parts. And further on, there is a description of all the fragments that were submitted for testing. I don't know whether there's any need for me to read all of this out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I believe not. I believe that everyone can read this. Actually, were you in a position to refer to the markings that you found on these fragments?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had there been any markings on any of these fragments, it probably would have been stated here. Even if only part of a particular marking could be seen, that was still referred to in the findings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: How could you recognise things, then?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of dimensions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can you tell us what dimensions led you to establish exactly what was what?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The metal fragments of cylindrical shapes, those were the bodies of the rocket motors, pipes. There's nothing else that would be similar to that. It's not that small that it couldn't be identified. These are bodies that had stabilisers on them. Some were more elaborate, some less, but it depended on the actual case involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: How can we understand this part that says "probably" and "most probably"? How should we read that? Was that established beyond a shade of doubt or is it most probably the case? Can we have 459, two pages. We have seen the findings - anyone can read that - but can we have the opinion? In the opinion, you stated the following: You said "most probably" or "probably." Last page in Serbian, please have a look at this, have a look at the opinion, and then tell us.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the opinion specifies what was established incontrovertibly. As for markings where there was no characteristic trace, then what was written was "most probably," et cetera. It says here: "Most probably originating from an aerial bomb." Further on, it says: "... the type of which cannot be established on the basis of the submitted material," because there were no characteristic traces or anything else on the basis of which the type or size of bomb could be established. However, there is no doubt that these are modified air-bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Actually, there is no doubt that what exists are rocket motors or, rather, the remains of these rocket motors. However, you cannot say anything about the actual warhead?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Things are the way they were written up. Those were the rocket motors, and probably the traces come from an air-bomb, and it is impossible to establish the type of air-bomb. That is what was established on the basis of the traces submitted for expertise. Also, there is a reference to some tin that probably made this a single compact whole.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This has already been admitted; right? It's part of a Prosecution exhibit, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, can I please ask you to tell me: What was the provenance of the weaponry and equipment of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give an answer to that because I don't know the answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Would you accept that professional military officers, and equipment and weapons, at least before the contingents arrived from Iran and other countries, actually originated from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where they came from later, but there's no doubt that the little bit that was there probably originated from the former Yugoslav People's Army. Now, did it come from some storage facilities that hadn't been emptied? I think that most of the weapons came from the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know and do you agree that all the ammunition in the storage facilities of the Yugoslav People's Army was subjected to compulsory overhaul after 15 to 20 years?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were compulsory overhauls, but I don't know what the actual period was. I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you accept that when they decided not to overhaul something, that then that kind of equipment would be destroyed or decommissioned?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they did with that. If it could not be overhauled, I don't know whether it was used further in production. I cannot speculate.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 09780.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can you tell us what type of document this is, and have you ever seen it before? Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report on a forensic on-site investigation, and it was prepared by the Forensics and KDZ Department. Here, it says, actually, "Public Security Station of Novi Grad municipality." And it's a report prepared by the investigators who conducted the on-site investigation. This is an investigation into an event of 26 May 1995, at Pavle Goranin District.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This is the incident that we were discussing earlier; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please read out the portion beginning with: "Two shells did not explode ..."? That's the third paragraph from the top.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Two shells did not explode. One ricochets, one struck the pavement and broke up. On the portion that did not explode, we found a fragment with swastika, and the shells probably come from World War II, which was established when inspected -- when the fragments were inspected." Now, if I may just add, this does not relate to the fragments of the projectiles that were submitted for testing or examination, because in the earlier part of the report it says that a projectile exploded on the roof of an apartment building in Safet Hadzic Street. And if I may just add something here. I recall, at least in one case, that we received for expertise fragments of these shells -- of this shell bearing the insignia of this eagle and the swastika on it, and when we researched literature, we established that this was an 88-millimetre artillery shell probably dating from World War II. Now, where and how this was launched, I don't know how it was fired, because I don't know that there were launch pads or launching devices of 88 millimetres, but they were probably fired from a 90-millimetre cannon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. May I just point you to the first part of the sentence. Is this that shell of -- a high-explosive shell that struck that building at number 52?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, these are two different shells, two other shells. They probably landed at about the same time, and the investigation team clearly said that. They said that one of the shell's fragments was sent for examination, and it was established that these were fragments of an air-bomb. And this is a different case, these shells, and I assume that these shells were 88-millimetre shells because we did not come across any other shells of this calibre. These were artillery-type shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this insignia -- or these markings, were they painted or were they printed into the metal?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, there was an imprint on the metal, but it was probably photographed. And I have to say that I didn't have an opportunity to see these photographs. But when I examined these fragments, I had occasion to see those fragments at the KDZ Department, where I worked at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Excellency, it would be very helpful if we could see -- if we could ask our learned friends to show us this photograph, to pull it up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I don't believe I've seen a photograph of a shell with a swastika and eagle on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, let me ask you this: This shell, other than this imprint that it had, were there any markings painted on it by applying paint?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know. I can't remember -- I don't remember. I can't really answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you agree that the Yugoslav People's Army had the duty, after each regular overhaul, to actually mark and put its own markings by painting a fragment or such assets that have been overhauled?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, the overhauled ordnance was painted, but I don't know how it was marked, exactly. It probably depended on the type of projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you then explain why it was not possible to identify, based on such a number, the provenance of these shells, because if they were from the Yugoslav People's Army's depots, then they would have had to bear that number of the regular overhaul or the general overhaul that was done on it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're asking me about things that I did not do, and no one ever asked us to establish anything of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, whom, then, should we attribute this shell to, Mr. Suljevic? Who did it belong to?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this shell can be attributed to those to whom we can attribute all the other shells that landed on the town of -- on the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. I will not go into that discussion here as to who fired what shells. But at this point, I would just like to confine our conversation to who or which side was the -- where was the provenance of these shells, and which of the sides had this type of shell, because this shell was probably from World War II, which would mean that it would have had to be overhauled twice, at least. So we have to attribute this shell to someone. We have to determine whose it was and whether it was from the JNA depots or not.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my point of view, there is absolutely no dispute about this shell having been fired from Serbian positions, because there were so many shells fired from there that I cannot believe that it was fired by Nazis. Now, during the war, there were two opposing sides, and, in my view, the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina did not fight its own ranks or the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, so they wouldn't have been able -- they couldn't have fired this shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you have any other evidence on which you base your conclusion that this was a Serb shell, other than that the BH Army did not fire on its own ranks or that it was imprecise?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have nothing to add, as far as this question is concerned.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I wonder if this report has already been admitted into evidence, or can we admit it now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D532, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now see 65 ter 09781, 09781.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: While we wait for this to come up: Mr. Suljevic, would you agree with me that in Safeta Hadzica Street, at number 102, some type of projectile landed, and this photo should depict that location? Do you recall we mentioned this number earlier, 102?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't recall -- I can't remember until I see the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it would appear that this was not in e-court, although this is a P number, and perhaps it's better to leave this on the screens because the quality is better. Or, rather, could we have this on the ELMO, please. It won't be perfect -- or maybe you have it in e-court. Now, if the Prosecution knows that this has already been up-loaded into e-court, perhaps we can get it. ERN 0037-5290.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I believe this is now in e-court under 09781, and it's just been released.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In that case, we will have it in e-court in a moment, and I believe it will be of better quality. Could we zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you recognise this location, Mr. Suljevic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, unless there was this caption beneath, I really couldn't guess what this might be, because this is a shed of some sort, a garage, there is a kind of garden behind, but that could be -- that could have been anywhere. But if we look at the caption, we can see that this was somewhere on Safeta Hadzica Street, but I cannot really affirm where exactly this is, nor can I even guess at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, is this a document that was used during the investigation done at the police? Is this something that you would commonly be using?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but this was done by the CSB members and their crime technicians, so this constituted part of the photo documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see where they put an arrow to indicate the point of impact of this shell?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can see the arrow. It's up on the shed, itself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we just have a much larger picture. Could we blow this up, this photo up, so that we could have a better view. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Suljevic, what type of shell, according to this report, landed here, causing this kind of damage here in this garden?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't see that there is much damage. But as far as I can see from the document we saw a moment ago, and we also see that there is a caption here, I believe that one of these artillery shells exploded here. And we can determine that and establish it if we look at the text above the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, you said this was not devastation, that there wasn't much damage. I was just really trying to make a joke. I mean, this looks more -- to me, it looks more like a shuttle exploding rather than a shell.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't comment on such statements, but you can see that there was a blast here. But the surface is such that you cannot really expect more devastation from that type of shell; if this was, for instance, a 90-millimetre shell or approximately so.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, don't you find it strange that the blast wave did not even move or displace the lettuce heads that we see there and that there is absolutely no trace of any damage on the wall of this hut? The only trace that we can see and find are the traces that are normally left behind if you shovel the ground, if you till the soil?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot really go into theoretical assumptions here, and I don't know when this projectile detonated. Maybe it detonated when it was already embedded in the soil, because obviously this is some kind of cabbage patch where -- I can't really go into assumptions as to how this might have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm a bit concerned about the transcript, because there was -- it did not enter in the transcript that the wire fence was not affected in any way. But I trust our interpreters to correct this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Suljevic, tell us, please: Any type of detonation, does that imply that there would also be an explosion of fragments and that they would fly in all directions; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. If an artillery shell explodes, that is the case, artillery shells that are meant for sowing destruction by shrapnel fragmentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, do we see any traces of shrapnel fragmentation on the wall of this shed?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really say for sure. Looking at the wall where the arrow was drawn, I can't claim anything about that. But I see to the left of that that there is some damage that could have been caused by shrapnel, but I am only assuming that based on what I see here. I did not actually conduct an investigation there. I did not go to the site, itself, so I can't say any more than what we can all see on this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. But you are familiar with these holes in these old slabs of concrete? These were just damages to the slabs of concrete?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was not really referring to these big holes on the slabs of concrete, on the blocks of concrete. I meant the minor -- the smaller holes. But it's possible that this was -- that these bigger holes, too, were caused by some kind of -- by fragments exploding. Perhaps some shells had fallen there earlier. I don't know, but we determine anything just based on this photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. But, in any case, one would expect that there would be fragmentation traces in the very vicinity of where a shell exploded and not further out?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, one would expect it to be there if a projectile detonated -- exploded above the surface of the ground. However, if the projectile explodes in the ground or underground, then we couldn't really expect that kind of damage. But looking at this photo, and I don't want to speculate here, but maybe we can see traces of some detonation and explosion on the right-hand side as well. But as I said, I don't really want to speculate. And as I've already said, one would expect -- when a projectile explodes above the surface or on the surface of the ground, one would expect to see traces of projectile debris or damage of projectile fragmentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you offer an explanation for the fact that the roof over the shed is intact? Do you really believe that the roof wouldn't have been blown away or damaged by the shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I would have to speculate in order to provide an answer. I don't know what was going on when the projectile landed. Some things sometimes defy logic, and those things did happen in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Would you expect, if such a huge projectile landed, the material of this roof, which is brittle and that's an asbestos roof, it should have been damaged?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a projectile explodes below the surface of the ground, then I wouldn't expect more damage than I can see here. Actually, I don't see any damage here on the asbestos boards.
