You can see that these are asbestos boards, but you don't see any damage on the boards because the roof is really horizontal; flat, almost. I don't know if there are any holes on the roof, itself. We can't see that, can we?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Suljevic. So neither the lettuce heads, nor the wire fence, nor the wall, nor the asbestos board, nothing is affected. Do you agree that the only thing that is missing in the photo is, actually, the shovel?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the painted wall. I don't want to proffer any comments. I can see just a shadow of the roof. And on the right-hand side, there are no boards. You can see points of damage. Based on the photo, I would not be able to make any inferences, and I don't want to do that, but it is obvious that here a lot of asbestos boards are missing. If you look at the photos, you will see the shadows of wooden beams. You can see the shadow of the asbestos roof on the left, and on the right-hand side you can only see beams, but not the asbestos boards, which means that they are missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: But will you agree with me that this is not immediately above the point of impact, it's a bit further away, it's probably a bit older? Wouldn't you expect that on the very place of the impact?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is above the place of the impact, because the furthest beam is around the crater or very close to the crater. It all depends on where the projectile came from, where the impact point was. From my point of view, this is something that could have been expected at the point of impact on the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. And if this explosion had damaged this roof, although we do not see it, would the fragments of the roof land somewhere around? They should be here, shouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you're asking me to speculate. I don't know whether roof fragments would be -- whether what we can see by the wall originates from the asbestos roof or not. If the impact wave came from the bottom, and if it hits the roof board, I suppose that that roof board would have been blown away. I'm speaking based on the photo, and I'm sharing my opinion with you. On the roof, on the right-hand side where the beams are, you can see some fragments of asbestos boards. I don't know whether it's just my impression. And then if you look on the left-hand side, you can see just a shadow, and the asbestos boards are not damaged. And in several places, you can see things. I suppose nobody climbed the roof to leave something on the roof. I suppose that something had landed on the roof, some fragments, as a result of explosion, either from the boards or just the soil.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: However, you, yourself, are not happy with the way the incident site was analysed and how things were processed?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. What do you expect from a photo, and what do you expect from a comment next to the photo?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, I expect that all traces would be depicted and help us to land at a conclusion. You, yourself, are saying that you have to resort to a lot of theoretical considerations. If the photo had been done correctly, everything should have been done clear, and if the description was better, then we wouldn't have to speculate or infer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You don't have to argue with the witness. We heard the evidence. Let's move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can the document please be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D533.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, within the next eight minutes I'm not in a position to complete the topic that I'm about to broach. I would like to remind you at this point why we wanted so much time for this important witness, because he can shed some light on crime investigations. And all the incidents have to be clarified before this Trial Chamber, and he is best suited to provide a good analysis of the incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We allowed you six hours to cross-examine Mr. Suljevic, and you have spent so far about a bit more than three hours. So after the recess, you will have three hours. But you do not expect to conclude your cross-examination in three hours' time; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I hoped that this witness -- or, rather, that the OTP has called this witness in order to prove the criminal and legal relevance of the incidents in the investigation of which he participated. And the Defence has a completely different task, and that is to show that the incidents transpired in a completely different way. We do have the basis to prove our case, we can prove our case, but if we're not allowed time to do it in the sufficient detail, we will not be able to do so. And that's why I don't think we will be able to complete the cross-examination of this witness within the next three hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was asking: How much longer do you need to conclude your cross-examination of this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will see how things go, but I am convinced that three hours is not enough. You see, yourself, that there are so many elements that have to be presented in respect of every single incident. We will see. I'll do my best to do things as fast as possible, but you will appreciate that this must not be done at the detriment of the Defence, or, rather, the Defence must not tie its own hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, Dr. Karadzic, that's a truism. But out of the last half hour, speaking for myself, about 25 minutes was spent asking this witness to speculate, which is not useful to anybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fine. We'll assess how much longer you would be given at the end of the six hours you will have. Mr. Suljevic, we find it very unfortunate not to be able to conclude your evidence before the summer recess which is forthcoming. We planned our trial schedule a long time ago, and we are unable to continue tomorrow, so I apologise. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the Court is aware of this or not, through -- either through VWS or any other source, but my understanding is it would be either impossible or an extreme inconvenience to the witness to return as soon as we convene. I gather he's available after the 20th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for the information. So on behalf of the Tribunal, I apologise for your inconvenience, that have you to travel to The Hague twice, but what happened happened. So I would ask you to return to The Hague, liaising with the Victim and Witness Section on the time which it would be convenient for you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. So is it correct that you are not able to come to The Hague before 20th of August?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is true, Your Honour. I've planned my summer holiday from the 2nd of August to sometime around the 20th, so, yes, it would be a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we'll liaise with you, through the Victim and Witness Section, and then the Prosecution will set an appropriate date in consultation with you. Thank you. You are free to go. Have a nice holiday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, I was wondering whether there's any administrative matters to be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be heard, Your Honour. The rhythm is fierce for the Defence, for myself, personally. I was hoping that we would be able to return to the regime of sitting of three days a week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I take it as a joke, Mr. Karadzic. We'll resume on 17th of August, at 9.00; that's Tuesday. And by that time, the Chamber hopes it would resolve the issue related to the scheduling of the hearing. And then I wish all the parties, and the staff as well, have a nice summer recess. We rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 17th day of August, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.29 p.m.,
